title: Eviction pattern safeguards and telemetry overhaul for prefix/KV cache
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
A production incident on 2026-02-22 revealed a sequence of correlated issues in the prefix/KV cache: an unusual eviction storm on a small subset of pods, transient cache poisoning by malformed session prefixes, and a latent reference-count memory leak in the shard cleanup code. The incident caused elevated latencies and degraded throughput for high-concurrency customers for ~45 minutes before fallback to disk-backed state reduced pressure.

Goals for this ticket:
1) Implement safeguards to prevent eviction storms from cascading (soft and hard eviction thresholds, exponential backoff on forced compactions).
2) Add defensive parsing and input sanitation where prefixes are deserialized to block cache poisoning vectors.
3) Patch reference-counting path and add deterministic shard GC to close the memory leak.
4) Roll out improved telemetry, alerting, and canary checks so similar regressions are detected before customer impact.

Non-goals:
- Full rewrite of the cache runtime. This ticket is focused on targeted mitigations, observability, and rollout controls.

Technical notes:
- Root cause analysis showed eviction storms were triggered by rapid key churn caused by our new routing policy plus a missing jitter in background compaction. Hot keys were intermittently moved between shards, causing thrashing in LRU lists.
- Cache poisoning exploited a corner case in prefix deserialization where non-UTF8 bytes led to a short-circuit path that skipped validation and allowed special control bytes in keys.
- The memory leak was introduced in shard_shrink() where a reference on value objects was not decremented under a specific error path; this only manifested under high shard-move rates.

Proposed solution (high level):
- Eviction safeguards: add a per-shard soft-eviction watermark that triggers background rebalancing instead of immediate aggressive evictions, track global eviction-rate metric and throttle compaction when we hit configurable thresholds.
- Deserialization defenses: centralize prefix parsing into a single vetted library with strict UTF-8 checking, length limits, and reject prefixes with control characters; add fuzz tests.
- Reference-count fix: ensure every early-return path in shard_shrink() decrements refs; add unit tests that simulate error paths. Convert some transient objects to arena-allocated lifetime where appropriate to simplify ownership.
- Telemetry and alerts: new metrics (evictions_per_shard, eviction_throttle_activations, prefix_parse_errors, refcount_incidents, shard_move_rate), dashboards, and PagerDuty alert rules for sustained eviction_rate > X/s for 5m.
- Deployment plan: small change set -> internal integration tests -> canary rollout to 3 pods in staging cluster -> staged production canary (5% traffic) -> full rollout with rollback gates.

Success criteria:
- No eviction storms across canary fleet for 72h under load tests that previously reproduced the incident.
- Prefix parse error rate drops to zero in production post-deploy.
- No memory growth beyond baseline for 1 week in canary and then in production monitoring.
